mentalModelCheck.question: How does Dialyzer success typing differ from traditional static type checkers (like Rust or TypeScript)?

options.label: Dialyzer requires 100% of variables to have explicit type annotations before compilation.
options.explanation: Dialyzer infers success types automatically even with zero annotations.

options.label: Dialyzer assumes all code is correct by default and only complains when it can mathematically prove that a function call will always fail.
options.explanation: Success typing works under the assumption that code is correct unless proven otherwise. Dialyzer only flags an error when it has mathematical certainty that a branch or call will always crash.

options.label: Dialyzer converts Erlang code into C++ before analyzing memory pointers.
options.explanation: Dialyzer analyzes BEAM Core Erlang bytecode directly.

options.label: Dialyzer runs tests with random mock inputs to observe crashes at runtime.
options.explanation: Dialyzer is a purely static analyzer; it never executes code.
